title.value: Multi-Environment Pretraining Enables Transfer to Action Limited Datasets
title.justification: The title of the paper describes a novel approach to enhance transfer learning in datasets with limited action annotations across different environments.
title.quote: Multi-Environment Pretraining Enables Transfer to Action Limited Datasets

extractions.description: The paper introduces Action Limited PreTraining (ALPT), a method that uses multi-environment pretraining to label missing action data in action-limited environments. By leveraging inverse dynamics modelling, the paper demonstrates improvement in generating action labels and enhancing game performance, even when using limited annotated datasets.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper presents innovative reinforcement learning techniques, it focuses on improving learning efficiencies in reinforcement learning tasks, specifically game-playing, rather than addressing environmental or sustainability challenges.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We show that utilizing even one additional environment dataset of labelled data during IDM pretraining gives rise to substantial improvements in generating action labels for unannotated sequences.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on reinforcement learning methodologies applicable to game-playing environments and does not specifically address any climate or ecological sustainable development objectives.
primary_category.quote: Our method, Action Limited PreTraining (ALPT), leverages the generalization capabilities of inverse dynamics modelling (IDM) to label missing action data in the target environment.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary relevance to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. The paper is largely centered on reinforcement learning methodologies for AI in gaming contexts.
secondary_categories.quote: While ALPT is, algorithmically, a straightforward application of existing offline RL approaches, our results provide a new perspective on large-scale training for RL. Namely, our results suggest that the most efficient path to large-scale RL methods may be via generalist inverse dynamics modelling paired with specialized agent finetuning, instead of generalist agent training alone.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper is about advancing methods in reinforcement learning for game environments, which do not fall under the existing sub-categories for sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose to circumvent this challenge by combining large but sparsely-annotated datasets from a target environment of interest with fullyannotated datasets from various other source environments.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The methodologies and objectives of this paper do not align with any specific sub-category because it focuses on general reinforcement learning improvements unrelated to sustainable development aspects.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our experiments and ablations highlight the importance of pretraining the IDM, as opposed to pretraining the DT agent alone.

applications.justification: The paper discusses applications in robotics and game-playing domains using the proposed ALPT method.
applications.quote: Recently, a number of works have shown that a similar approach can be applied to tasks more often tackled by reinforcement learning (RL), such as robotics and game-playing.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not necessitate a new category as it does not address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose Action Limited Pretraining (ALPT), which relies on the hypothesis that shared structures between environments can be exploited by non-causal (i.e., bidirectional) transformer IDMs.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no new sub-category needed, as the work does not relate to sustainable development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: ALPT thus uses the multienvironment source datasets as pretraining for an IDM, which is then finetuned on the action-limited data of the target environment in order to provide labels for the unlabelled target data, which is then used for training a DT agent.
